name: George W. Harmon
bio: George W. Harmon was sheriff of Morton County. From the summer of 1885 he came to town to empanel jurors, serve warrants and post election notices, and he gave the Cow Boy figures on what it would cost to organize Billings County. At the September 1885 trial of the Marquis de Mores, a witness named Harmon testified to hearing Luffsey and O'Donald threaten to shoot de Mores, and Howard Eaton testified he had been sent to meet the sheriff before the shooting. Harmon also advertised sheriff's sales, one at the Cantonment near Medora in 1885 and an 1886 foreclosure sale of Medora property of John and Mary Kiefer, held at Mandan. In October 1886 the Morton County Republican convention nominated him again for sheriff.
